title: Nadia and Fahri Negotiate the Wedding Guest List
script: Nadia: [stressed] Fahri, your mother wants to invite forty more relatives, and my parents are already stretching the budget as generously as they can.
Fahri: [apologetic] I know, and I'm embarrassed by how entitled the request sounds, especially since half of them barely acknowledge our family otherwise.
Nadia: [gently] I'm not blaming you. I just don't know how to decline gracefully without implying we consider them unimportant.
Fahri: [thoughtful] What if we framed it around venue capacity rather than preference? That way, nobody feels personally excluded, only logistically constrained.
Nadia: [considering] That's diplomatic, though your mother might still read between the lines and feel wounded regardless of how we phrase it.
Fahri: [honestly] She might, but I'd rather she feel briefly disappointed than have your parents feel financially cornered into hosting strangers.
Nadia: [relieved] Thank you for saying that plainly. I worried you'd default to appeasing her at my family's expense, like last time.
Fahri: [reflective] That's fair criticism, and I've been thinking about it since. Adab shouldn't mean constantly yielding to whoever complains loudest.
Nadia: [softening] Exactly. It should mean weighing everyone's dignity fairly, not just avoiding the most uncomfortable conversation in the room.
Fahri: [determined] Alright. I'll speak with her myself, respectfully but firmly, and explain the numbers honestly instead of hiding behind vague excuses.
Nadia: [warmly] Would it help if I joined that conversation, or would my presence make her feel outnumbered and defensive?
Fahri: [considering] Maybe join partway through, once I've explained the reasoning. That way it looks like solidarity, not confrontation.
Nadia: [thoughtful] That seems wise. I don't want her to feel ganged up on, even while we're holding a firm boundary.
Fahri: [warmly] We can hold the boundary and still honor her feelings. Those two things aren't actually in conflict, whatever it feels like right now.
Nadia: [softly] I hope she hears it that way. Either way, I'm grateful we're facing this together instead of separately resenting each other.

quiz.question: What is the central disagreement about?
options: Which venue to choose
Whether to invite forty more relatives that Fahri's mother wants added
What food to serve at the wedding
When the wedding should happen
quiz.explanation: Fahri's mother wants to invite forty more relatives, straining the budget Nadia's parents are already stretching.

quiz.question: What framing does Fahri suggest for declining the extra guests?
options: Saying the relatives are not liked
Framing it around venue capacity rather than personal preference
Blaming Nadia's parents entirely
Cancelling the wedding
quiz.explanation: Fahri suggests framing the decline around venue capacity so nobody feels personally excluded, only logistically constrained.

quiz.question: What criticism does Nadia raise about Fahri's past behavior?
options: That he never talks to his mother
That he worried he'd default to appeasing his mother at Nadia's family's expense
That he refuses to compromise ever
That he ignores wedding planning entirely
quiz.explanation: Nadia says she worried Fahri would default to appeasing his mother at her family's expense, like a previous time.

quiz.question: What does Fahri decide to do about speaking with his mother?
options: Avoid the conversation entirely
Speak with her himself, respectfully but firmly, explaining the numbers honestly
Ask his father to handle it instead
Send her a text message
quiz.explanation: Fahri decides to speak with his mother himself, respectfully but firmly, explaining the budget honestly instead of vague excuses.

quiz.question: How do they plan for Nadia to join the conversation?
options: She won't join at all
She'll join partway through, so it looks like solidarity rather than confrontation
She'll start the conversation alone
She'll only send a written note
quiz.explanation: They agree Nadia will join partway through, once Fahri has explained the reasoning, so it reads as solidarity rather than confrontation.
